sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A survey table records: group X with 4 successes and 20 failures; group Y with 9 successes and 24 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 3/10, P(B) = 7/10, and P(A and B) = 26/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).

items.prompt: In a group of 20, 8 do activity A, 13 do activity B, and 4 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 5/8 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 43 successes and 43 failures; group Y with 30 successes and 40 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 8/10, P(B) = 4/10, and P(A and B) = 32/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.

items.prompt: In a group of 41, 13 do activity A, 13 do activity B, and 2 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 2/9 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 26 successes and 19 failures; group Y with 7 successes and 32 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
